newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescuers pull survivor from Australian landslide.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers pull survivor from Australian landslide.

text.p: Rescuers on Saturday pulled a survivor from the wreckage of two Australian ski lodges almost three days after the buildings were engulfed by a landslide.

Ski instructor Stuart Diver, 27, was lifted out of a small hole in the rubble on a stretcher and quickly covered with several blankets before being carried up a steep slope by rescue workers to a waiting ambulance.
Diver was found around dawn on Saturday entombed between huge concrete slabs after a fireman heard a muffled voice.
Rescuers, digging by hand so as not to dislodge the concrete slab, took 11 hours to free him.
Officials said he was in serious but stable condition, suffering hypothermia and lacerations, but was in good spirits.
The death toll in the landslide rose to six on Saturday with the discovery of three more bodies. Thirteen people are missing.
They were buried under tonnes of soil, rock and trees on Wednesday night when the slide hit the Thredbo Alpine Village in the Snowy Mountains, 400 km (250 miles) south of Sydney.
